newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia sets life insurance consumer rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia sets life insurance consumer rules.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday it would introduce consumer protection measures for life insurance.

"The proposed measures include provisions comparable to the corporations law in relation to product disclosure requirements, prohibition on deceptive and misleading conduct, adviser recommendations, and remedies and sanctions," Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp said in a statement.
Life insurance companies would have to form compliance committees to boost accountability to their clients, Kemp said.
The committees would also monitor company compliance with disclosure requirements, the Code of Practice and other consumer related measures, he said.
Reserve powers would be provided under the Life Insurance Act 1995 to allow the watchdog Insurance and Superannuation Commission to give statutory backing if the consumer protection measures failed.

"These reforms will raise industry standards of service and advice and thereby give consumers greater confidence when considering life insurance products as protection against adversity and investments for the future," Kemp said.
